claims.claim: A 10-year follow-up of nearly 10,000 older women found that drinking more than five cups of coffee daily was linked to lower hip bone density while tea consumption correlated with slightly higher density.
claims.episode_span: A 10-year study of nearly 10,000 older women ties drinking more than five cups of coffee daily to lower hip bone density while moderate tea intake links to slightly higher density.
claims.source_title: Too much coffee may weaken bones, study finds
claims.supporting_quote: Following nearly 10,000 older women for 10 years, researchers found that tea drinking was associated with slightly higher hip bone density. Moderate coffee consumption did not appear harmful, but drinking more than five cups a day was linked to lower bone density.

claims.claim: Obesity appears to leave a molecular imprint on key immune cells that may persist for 5 to 10 years after weight loss.
claims.episode_span: Obesity appears to leave a durable molecular signature on immune cells that can persist for years after weight returns to normal.
claims.source_title: Obesity leaves a lasting memory in immune cells
claims.supporting_quote: Obesity appears to leave a molecular imprint on key immune cells that may persist for 5 to 10 years after weight loss.
